07 - Calibrating Hedonic Pricing Model for Private Highrise Property with GWR Method

Author

Cathy C.

Published

October 17, 2025

Modified

October 17, 2025

1 Overview

Geographically weighted regression (GWR) is a spatial statistical technique that takes non-stationary variables into consideration (e.g., climate; demographic factors; physical environment characteristics) and models the local relationships between these independent variables and an outcome of interest (also known as dependent variable). In this hands-on exercise, we will build hedonic pricing models by using GWR methods. The dependent variable is the resale prices of condominium in 2015. The independent variables are divided into either structural and locational.

Note

Non-stationary variables = Things that change depending on where you are.

The two types of factors:

  • Structural factors - Physical features of the condo itself (size, number of rooms, age of building, facilities)
  • Locational factors - Where the condo is located (distance to MRT station, nearby schools, shopping centers)

Hedonic pricing = identifies price factors based on the idea that a good’s price is influenced by both its internal characteristics and external factors. Hedonic pricing is often used to estimate the value of environmental or ecosystem services that influence home prices. This valuation method often requires statistical expertise and model specification after collecting data.
